You gotta play chicken with them and win. Which isn't that hard once you understand that they are not an oncoming vehicle. They'll always split up or dodge off the road if you hold steady because they definitely won't survive a head on collision.

I have a question however. Is it implied that charging these creatures and simply not stopping is a way of avoiding an encounter with them? Or would they run you off the road anyhow?

item.content:encoded: Wait, this is a total necro, but did anyone realize what this guy said? This is EXACTLY like the stories of things that pretended to be lanterns to lead people into marshes in order to kill them, but they've gradually evolved to hunt in pairs, move faster, glow brighter, and camoflauge themselves with the night in order to adapt to people inventing cars. Which means that eventually, when we have hovercrafts, these motherfuckers are going to be able to fly.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I liked this when I read it, I liked it even more when I read that diary entry, and it got an upvote from me, no question. There are a couple of minor things that bug me though.

First off, the sentence "SCP-745's genetic structure is not carbon based." I understand why this is here, but the placement of the sentence feels blunt and a little jarring. I'm sure there's a way it could be integrated a little better.

Also, the phrase "the child-like hand prints from SCP-745's front paws" doesn't seem very clinical, at least where it is. I feel like the description of the handprints as child-like should be alongside the other physical attributes. I admit, though, I can't think of another way to get across the creep factor of the handprints.

Like I said, I like this, and 42 other upvotes can't be wrong. These are just a couple of things that jumped out at me.
